# Txtrvl

> A responsive text animation library for React, built around the named Txtrvl component.

Install with `npm install txtrvl`. Import with `import { Txtrvl } from "txtrvl"`.
The `text` prop accepts a string. The optional `animation` prop selects `reveal`,
`fade`, `slide-up`, `slide-left`, `blur`, or `scale`; `reveal` is the default.
Timing values are in milliseconds: `duration` defaults to 1000 and `delayPerRow`
to 200. Text follows browser line wrapping and updates with container resizing
and font loading. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.

## Documentation

- [README and API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichalKowalczyk/Txtrvl/master/README.md): Installation, examples, options, Next.js usage, and performance limitations.
- [Component and public types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichalKowalczyk/Txtrvl/master/src/Txtrvl/Txtrvl.tsx): Source of truth for TxtrvlProps and TxtrvlAnimation.
- [Package metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichalKowalczyk/Txtrvl/master/package.json): Version, peer dependencies, and module entry points.
- [Interactive examples](https://txtrvl.com/): Demo website. Refer to the README and public types for the current API.

## Usage notes

Automatic scroll triggering is enabled by default. For manual playback alone,
use `scrollTrigger={{ disabled: true }}` and `manualTrigger={{ isVisible }}`.
`offsetY` changes the vertical detection bounds. An optional ancestor DOM element
can be passed as `scrollTrigger.root`. Next.js entry points include `"use client"`;
callbacks and interactive state belong in a Client Component.

Do not use a default import, `animationType`, or `speed`: they are not part of
the public API. Apply text color and typography through `style` or `className`.
